standard.title: Locate and process information in texts
standard.description: locate and process information and ideas in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate, organise and respond to key information in familiar texts across multiple sources (AC9LCH4C03). They can retell, summarise and present findings. They have not yet processed texts analytically — identifying author perspective, cultural positioning, or variations in language register — or responded in ways that are deliberately adapted for different purposes and audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate and process information and ideas in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts — including analysing perspective and language variation — and respond in different ways appropriate to purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Analysing perspective and language variation in texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify variations in language use across texts — including tone, register, word choice and perspective — and discuss what these reveal about the text's purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of language variation (tone, register, or word choice) in a text and explain what each suggests about purpose or audience.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe key elements of texts including perspective, language variation, setting, character and event; analyse how language choices reflect purpose and audience; compare language use across different text types and media contexts.
wider: Compare how the same topic or event is represented in two different texts — identify differences in perspective, language choices and what is emphasised or omitted, and discuss why
Analyse a text from a First Nations Australian author — identify the perspective and values embedded in the language choices and compare with the student's own cultural perspective
nodes.hinge_reason: Analytical text processing is the prerequisite for response that is genuinely adapted to purpose and audience. Students who can only retrieve information cannot evaluate perspective, identify language variation, or make deliberate response choices — the core demands of this descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Perspective and language variation analysis requires explicit analytical frameworks — students need prompts to move from 'this is what the text says' to 'this is how and why the language was chosen.' Guided analysis with explicit discussion questions develops this capacity before students can analyse independently.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two examples of language variation in a text
Explains what at least one language choice reveals about the text's purpose or audience

nodes.label: Processing and responding to imaginative and cultural texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read, view or listen to imaginative texts in the target language and respond — including through performance, discussion or creative response — demonstrating understanding of content and cultural context.
nodes.minimum_width: Read, view or listen to an imaginative text and produce at least one response (performance, discussion, or creative work) demonstrating understanding of content and at least one cultural element.
nodes.typical_width: Read, view or listen to imaginative texts — poems, stories, folk tales, cartoons, films — and respond through performance, discussion or creative work; identify cultural context and language choices; connect texts to personal experience and cultural background; explore migration stories and cross-cultural perspectives.
wider: Create a performance or creative response that reimagines a key scene or moment in a familiar text from a different cultural perspective
Compare the cultural values embedded in a target language imaginative text with those of an equivalent Australian text — discuss what the comparison reveals about cultural difference and similarity

response_modes.reason: Response to imaginative texts develops through encounter with a range of text types and cultural contexts. Students who have responded to only one type of imaginative text cannot generalise their response strategies. Varied text encounters — different genres, media, cultural contexts — build flexible response capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners bring cultural and personal resonance to target language imaginative texts that peers without this background cannot access. Width investment — particularly in tasks that draw on migration stories and family cultural experience — activates this unique perspective and produces responses of genuine cultural depth.
success_criteria: Produces a response to an imaginative text demonstrating understanding of content
Identifies at least one cultural element in the text and connects it to their own experience or knowledge

nodes.label: Responding to suit purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce a response to a text that is deliberately adapted for purpose and audience — selecting format, language and content appropriate to the communicative context.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one response to a text that demonstrates a clear deliberate choice about format, language or content appropriate to a specific purpose or audience.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to informative and imaginative texts in different ways for different purposes and audiences — summaries, discussions, performances, creative responses, presentations; adapt language register, format and content to suit the response context; compare information across texts and present findings.
wider: Produce two different responses to the same text for different audiences — for example, a summary for a peer and a performance for younger students — then compare the language and format choices made in each
Create a multimodal response to a text that combines language, image and another mode — explain how each mode contributes to the overall meaning and why this format suits the purpose

response_modes.reason: Purposeful, audience-aware response integrates analytical text processing (node 1) and imaginative text engagement (node 2) into a full communicative act. The teaching investment is in making audience and purpose explicit as design decisions — not default choices — before students produce their response.

success_criteria: Produces a response demonstrating at least one deliberate language or format choice appropriate to audience or purpose
Can explain the choice made and why it suits the communicative context
